Preserve existing billing when nested details are absent, along with exi

lessons: A nested modality split changes how cache reads are allocated; it must not bypass the existing budget for uncached input. Trace generic_cost_per_token through parsing and _calculate_input_cost, then the reported token-cost breakdown. After subtracting cache reads and cache writes from aggregate input, full-rate modality buckets must fit the remaining budget. Count every token once; cache-creation tokens must not also receive the ordinary input charge.

For a changed cache/modality path, check one mixed case with nonzero cache writes, not only the new example and isolated old cache-write tests. Use the current task’s rates and existing public billing entrypoints. Distinguish an absent audio-cache rate from explicit zero, and compare total and breakdown amounts. Keep the no-nested-split path, tier/region/custom-price behavior and caller-owned input intact. This is a review hypothesis, not a requirement to add unrelated behavior or rerun a broad suite.
